h1: The 7 Best Portable Spot Cleaners for Couches and Upholstery in 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Spot Cleaners for Couches: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 portable spot cleaners for sofas and upholstery from BISSELL, Hoover, Shark and Uwant, compared on tools and moisture control.
mainKeyword: portable spot cleaners for couches and upholstery
summary: The Hoover CleanSlate XL is the spot cleaner to buy if the target is a whole sofa, with a deep-cleaning design aimed at full-size furniture. The BISSELL Little Green Max Pet leads on controlled moisture and pickup, the Shark StainStriker brings four tools in different widths, and the Little Green Mini is the cushion-crevice specialist.
intro: Couches punish the wrong machine in a way carpets do not. A sofa cushion is thick foam wrapped in fabric, and any machine that leaves it soaking can produce a water ring, a musty smell and a stain that comes back as the foam dries. The point of a good upholstery cleaner is therefore not power at all, it is how little water stays behind.

That is the lens for this ranking. We sorted seven portable machines by moisture control, tool shape for cushions, seams and arms, and how much fabric each can reasonably handle in one session. We reviewed product listings, not furniture, and always point you to the cleaning code on your sofa tag first.

products.name: Hoover CleanSlate XL Deep Cleaning Carpet + Upholstery Spot Cleaner Machine
products.verdict: A deep-cleaning spot machine sized for whole sofas rather than single chairs.
products.description:
The CleanSlate XL is the larger sibling in Hoover's spot cleaner line, positioned as a deep-cleaning carpet and upholstery machine. It is aimed at people cleaning a full sofa or sectional rather than a single armchair, and falls in the $100 to $200 tier.

The case for first place is scale. A sofa has several seat cushions, back cushions and arm panels, and a machine meant for bigger jobs carries more solution per tank, so you stop less often. It trades portability for that capacity, and it is heavier to carry up a flight of stairs than the Mini.

Buy it if you plan to clean entire sofas or a sectional. Skip it if you only do single chairs and car seats.

products.name: BISSELL Little Green Max Pet Portable Carpet Cleaner, 3860
products.verdict: Strong pickup with controlled moisture output, which is what couches need.
products.description:
The Max Pet is the top BISSELL Little Green for pet households, and it is described as combining strong pickup with controlled moisture output. For a sofa, those two traits are the whole recipe: lift the dirt, leave the foam nearly dry.

It sits just behind the Hoover XL, which wins on size, but it beats it on pet performance and on how easy it is to store. It costs $100 to $200. Pet urine on upholstery is the hardest job in this category, because the liquid soaks into foam, and a tool that extracts well matters more than a big tank.

Buy it if a dog or cat uses your furniture. Skip it if you want the largest capacity.

products.name: Shark StainStriker Portable Carpet/Upholstery Cleaner, 4 Tools, PX202BRN
products.verdict: Four tools in different widths cover cushions, arms and seams.
products.description:
The StainStriker ships with four tools, which the listing points to as the draw for buyers cleaning furniture of different shapes. Upholstery has wide cushion faces, narrow seams and curved arms, and no single head does all three well.

It ranks third because the Hoover and the BISSELL Max Pet outrank it on size and moisture control, but the tool range gives it a flexibility they lack. The extra attachments mean more cleanup after each session. It costs $100 to $200.

Buy it if your furniture includes a mix of shapes. Skip it if you want a single, simple tool.
products.idealFor: Mixed furniture with cushions, arms and seams.
products.skipIf: You want a single simple tool.

products.name: BISSELL Little Green Multi-Purpose Portable Carpet Cleaner, 1400B
products.verdict: The long-running Little Green that owners trust for upholstery.
products.description:
The 1400B is the multi-purpose Little Green that built the brand's reputation, and the listing calls it the most proven upholstery-safe design here. It costs $100 to $200.

It ranks fourth because its simplicity is both its strength and its limit. Proven is a real advantage for couch cleaning, since a machine with a long track record is less likely to surprise you with leaks or drips. It lacks the pet tooling of the Max Pet and the capacity of the Hoover XL.

Buy it if you want a reliable general machine for sofas. Skip it if you have heavy pet messes.
products.idealFor: Reliable general cleaning of fabric furniture.
products.skipIf: Pet messes are the main job.

products.name: BISSELL Little Green Pet Deluxe Portable Carpet Cleaner, 3353
products.verdict: A pet-focused Little Green for furniture that sees regular pet contact.
products.description:
The Pet Deluxe 3353 is a pet-focused Little Green, positioned for owners whose couches and chairs get regular pet contact. It costs $100 to $200.

It ranks fifth because the Max Pet above it is the stronger pet machine, and this model overlaps heavily with it. Pet fur and body oils build up on armrests and cushion edges, and a pet-targeted tool helps with both. If you find it at a good price it is a perfectly sound alternative.

Buy it if you want a pet-focused model and the Max Pet is out of stock. Skip it if you have no pets.
products.idealFor: Pet owners whose sofas get daily contact.

products.name: Uwant Carpet Cleaner Machine 18Kpa Portable Carpet Cleaner for Cars Couch, 2in1 Water Tank
products.verdict: A budget 18Kpa spot cleaner with a two-in-one water tank for cars and couches.
products.description:
The Uwant lists 18Kpa suction, a two-in-one water tank for upholstery, spot cleaning and a tools set. It costs $50 to $100 and targets budget-conscious buyers who want fabric-safe cleaning.

It ranks sixth because the brand is less established than the BISSELL and Hoover options, and the 18Kpa suction figure is a manufacturer claim. The two-in-one tank layout is a handy design that separates clean and dirty water. On a couch it is fine for light stains.

Buy it if you want the lowest price for occasional couch and car seat cleaning. Skip it if you need proven service.
products.idealFor: Occasional couch and car seat cleaning.

products.name: BISSELL Little Green Mini Portable Carpet Cleaner, 4075
products.verdict: A compact machine for cushion crevices and small chairs.
products.description:
The Mini 4075 is the compact Little Green, described as a tool for cushion crevices. It costs $50 to $100 and is easy to carry from room to room.

It ranks last because a small machine means more refills when you clean a whole sofa. Where it shines is the tight corner where a bigger head cannot reach: the gap between cushion and arm, the seam of a dining chair, a car seat. Think of it as a second machine, or the only one for a small apartment.

Buy it if you have limited storage or mostly clean small pieces. Skip it if you have a large sectional.
products.idealFor: Small furniture, car seats and apartments.

whatMatters.detail: Furniture tags carry a letter code. W means water-based cleaners are safe, S means solvent only, WS means either, and X means vacuum only. A water-based spot cleaner suits W and WS fabrics only, so check the tag under a cushion first.

Cushions hold water in their foam, and a wet cushion can take a day to dry and develop a ring. Controlled moisture and strong suction matter more than tank size. Make several light passes rather than one wet one.
A wide tool covers cushions fast, while a narrow tool reaches seams and crevices. Having both saves time and avoids flooding a small spot. Count the tools in the box.
Stiff bristles can fuzz or damage delicate fabrics such as velvet or microfibre. Look for tools with softer rubber or short bristle options. Test a hidden area before cleaning the whole sofa.
Some formulas leave residue that attracts dirt, and strong ones can fade dye. Use the maker's upholstery formula or plain water for light jobs. Rinse with clean water and recover.

cards.text: Controlled moisture, soft tool edges, and a maker that names upholstery use. Always test a hidden area and obey the cleaning code.

faq.q: Can I use a carpet spot cleaner on a couch?
faq.a: Yes, if the fabric's cleaning code allows water-based cleaning (W or WS) and you use an upholstery tool. Test a hidden area first.
Soaking the cushion. Make light passes, recover as much liquid as you can, and let the cushion dry with airflow to avoid rings and smells.

faq.q: Is the Hoover XL worth it over a Little Green?
faq.a: If you clean whole sofas or sectionals, yes, because of the larger design. For spot cleaning and pets, a Little Green is easier to store and use.
Fill the clean tank, attach the hose and upholstery tool, plug in, and start with a hidden patch. It takes a few minutes.

faq.q: How long does a couch take to dry?
faq.a: Several hours at least, longer with thick cushions. Use a fan and open windows, and avoid sitting on damp cushions.

faq.q: Can I clean velvet or microfibre?
faq.a: Be careful. Some velvets mark with water, so check the tag and test a hidden spot. A professional is safer for delicate or valuable pieces.

finalTake: For whole sofas, the Hoover CleanSlate XL is the best portable spot cleaner for couches and upholstery here. The BISSELL Little Green Max Pet is the pick for pet households and controlled moisture, and the Shark StainStriker adds tool variety. Read the cleaning code on your sofa tag first, and always clean light, recover well and dry with airflow.
